claim: At 18 kN vertical load after 1524 m, a bias-ply tire showed little carcass-temperature difference between 25% and 30% vertical deflection but a significant increase at 35%.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.

claim: The extended free-roll test reported equilibrium inner-wall temperatures above 121 C over multiple crown/sidewall stations; the paper warns this can cause premature failure.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.

claim: Cornering-force coefficient per degree decreased from 0.041/deg at 20% rated vertical load to 0.022/deg at 75% rated load for the tested tilted tire.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.

claim: For the reported rolling test, 848 W of friction work at 22.35 m/s corresponded to 37.9 N road resistance, with 4448 N load and 0.02421 m2 footprint.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.

claim: The paper estimated 64% of absorbed power from tread-surface squirm/sliding and 36% from hysteresis for its bias-ply belted test tire.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.

claim: A thermal estimate reduced hysteresis-induced drag from about 89 N at 40-60 s to about 21.6 N after roughly 1000 s near thermal equilibrium.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.

claim: At 38 C contained-air temperature, rolling-resistance coefficients were reported for two tire sets at 207 and 276 kPa.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.

claim: Average contained-air equilibrium time was 20 min for constant-speed tests and 27 min for the Schedule D cycle; average rolling-resistance change from startup to equilibrium was 5%.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.

claim: Wet-braking effectiveness degraded gradually to about 80% tread wear, then degraded much more sharply from 80% to 100% wear.
applicability: Wet-tread degradation shape and observable separation; not a dry racing grip-life curve.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.

claim: Across tests spanning 24-150 psi, 45-120 mph and 125-22,000 lb, the reported incipient-hydroplaning lift coefficient was approximately 0.7.
applicability: General wet-model validation only; not a racing dry-pressure prior.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
